title: apply_fx_destructively result
description: What apply_fx_destructively returns: which items had the chain rendered into their audio, and whether the original take survived. replacedExistingTake is the field that says how recoverable this is — a new take leaves the original alongside the processed audio, replacing it does not, and REAPER's undo is then the only way back. The items are named by GUID because rendering a take mints new take audio and the producer needs to be told which of their items were changed, not just how many. A mutating tool, so it carries the undo report fields defined by messages/tool-result-undo.schema.json.

processedItemGuids.description: The items whose audio now contains the FX chain, in timeline order. Every item on the track when the call named none.

replacedExistingTake.description: True when the processed audio replaced the take that was there, false when it was added as a new take alongside the original. The producer's route back differs entirely between the two, so this is not a restatement of the input.

appliedFxCount.description: How many FX from the chain were rendered in. Bypassed FX are not applied, so this can be lower than the chain length — and a producer who bypassed a plugin to audition without it would not expect it baked in.

trackReference.description: A track the tool acted on, named as well as identified. The GUID is what the agent addresses the track by on any follow-up call; the name is what it says to the producer, who cannot see a GUID. Returned even when the call supplied a GUID, because a name pattern resolves here rather than in the agent — a safe operation on a confident-but-imperfect match proceeds and this is how it reports which track it chose (Requirement 7.6).

name.description: Track name as shown in REAPER at the time of the call.

guid.description: A stable REAPER GUID, in REAPER's own braced form.

undoPositionBefore.description: REAPER undo stack position captured by the extension immediately before this tool applied its change. A "revert all AI changes" operation calls Undo_DoUndo2 in a loop until the stack is back at this position.

undoDescription.description: Undo point description the extension passed to Undo_EndBlock2 for this tool, persisted with the tool_result message so the chat UI can list what the agent changed.
